title: Driver Quality Bulletin: Numbering of Cancellation-Rate Warnings on Wayfare Agreements
content:
Every cancellation-rate warning recorded on a **Driver Services Agreements and Account Standing** agreement carries a number.

## The rule

The cancellation warning sequence number is the number a cancellation-rate warning carries within the driver's current warning cycle. A cancellation-rate warning continues the numbering of the driver's warning cycle: its cancellation warning sequence number is the sequence number of the latest earlier cancellation-rate warning on the standing record plus one, or one when the standing record holds no earlier cancellation-rate warning.

The warning records the cancellation rate shown at the latest rating review on the standing record.

## Reading the standing record

| What the standing record shows | Number of the new cancellation-rate warning |
|---|---|
| no earlier cancellation-rate warning | 1 |
| latest earlier cancellation-rate warning numbered 1 | 2 |
| latest earlier cancellation-rate warning numbered 3 | 4 |

- Only cancellation-rate warnings are read for the number; a rating warning is not a cancellation-rate warning.
- "Latest" means the most recent by date.
- No rounding applies; the number is a whole number.

## Worked example (hypothetical record)

A driver's standing record shows cancellation-rate warnings numbered 1 (dated 2026-05-04) and 2 (dated 2026-07-20), a rating warning dated 2026-08-01, and rating reviews whose latest shows a cancellation rate of 11.3 percent. The new cancellation-rate warning is numbered 3 (the latest earlier cancellation-rate warning is number 2), and it records 11.3.
